anna_chen: Heads-up — bringing up lynx-v2-mini (q4f) on staging and our short-JA embedding checks are weird. Small inputs with a zero-width-space between katakana and kanji are getting mapped to different token ids vs the fp16 baseline. cosine(sim_fp16, sim_q4f) for a couple samples is ~0.62 which seems too low. Anyone seen ZWSP/katakana swaps after quant?

josh_gold: Can you paste a minimal repro (input + token ids before/after)? Also which tokenizer version? :eyes:

anna_chen: Sure — tokenizer v2.3.1 (we vendor it in runtime). Example: input has a ZWSP (U+200B) between カナ and 漢. Repro commands I ran:

```
# inspect tokens (fp16 model)
python -m rn_tokenizer.inspect --model lynx-v2-mini --mode fp16 --text "カナ漢"
# inspect tokens (q4f)
python -m rn_tokenizer.inspect --model lynx-v2-mini --mode q4f --text "カナ漢"
```

FP16 tokens: ["カナ", "漢"] ids: [2345, 9872]
Q4F tokens: ["カナ", "漢"] ids: [2345, 45123]  <-- notice second id differs (45123)

mei_lin: that's odd. So the token boundaries differ: the ZWSP is attached to the katakana in q4f. That would shift tokenization and thus embeddings. Did the tokenizer vocabulary change between quant builds?

anna_chen: We pinned vocab, so shouldn't. My hunch: kernel-level normalization/byte-level path in the quantized tokenizer runtime is treating ZWSP as part of preceding grapheme cluster. We also saw mismatch for thin-space vs ZWSP.

kaan_erdem: Could be different unicode normalization upstream. Quant runtime uses a faster fallback that skips NFKC for performance in q4f builds unless configured. Check if compile flag `--enable-normalize` was set for q4f.

anna_chen: Good call. I checked build meta: q4f serving image was built with FLAG_NORMALIZE=0 (for speed). fp16 image had it enabled.

josh_gold: That explains token differences. Two quick questions: 1) why cosine so low (0.62) — is it purely token shift or also embedding table reordering in quant? 2) How many samples affected?

mei_lin: I ran a small batch (n=120 short JA queries). Breakdown: ~18% show token boundary shift when ZWSP/ZWJ present, BLEU delta small (<0.5) for translation tasks but embedding cosine median drops from 0.92->0.78 for those affected samples. So token shift accounts for most of metric delta.

anna_chen: Also noticed an embedding-table alignment mismatch for some ids > 32768 in q4f, but that's a separate weirdness — likely id remap at quant export. For now the normalization mismatch is the biggest source.

deploy-bot: started job lynx-v2-mini-q4f-repro-1717123456 (staging)

kaan_erdem: Short-term mitigation: normalize inputs to NFKC and strip ZWSP before tokenizing in the platform preprocessor. Perf hit negligible at request scale. Long-term: re-enable normalization in q4f tokenizer runtime or make it opt-on with config per deployment.

anna_chen: I pushed a quickfix to the staging preprocessor: strip_zwsp=true and run the regression suite. Quick script I used to patch:

```
# one-liner preproc
python -c "import sys;print(sys.stdin.read().replace('\u200b',''))" < samples.txt | rn_eval embeddings --model lynx-v2-mini-q4f
```

Result: cosine med for affected samples rose to 0.89 after strip_zwsp (was 0.78). BLEU unaffected.

josh_gold: Ok good. Can you open a short RFC/ticket to decide on default: strip ZWSP vs enable normalization in runtime? Also we should add a unit test for ZWSP/ZWJ and thin-space cases in our tokenizer test suite.

anna_chen: Filing ticket now: INF-4892 "ZWSP/ZWJ handling mismatch in q4f tokenizer" with repro and perf notes. Assigning to eng-ml and eng-runtime.

mei_lin: For the longer-term quant export issue (id remap >32768) I'll run a bisect on the export pipeline — could be an off-by-one in our remap table when switching to 16-bit index packing. Will report back.

kaan_erdem: Thanks — add a smoke check in the quant packer to assert id space preserved.

anna_chen: TL;DR: root cause = normalization disabled in q4f runtime -> token boundary shifts for invisible chars (ZWSP/ZWJ) -> embedding deltas. Mitigation = strip ZWSP in preprocessor + ticket to re-enable/opt-in normalization in quant runtime. Planning: roll preproc patch to Dedicated canary today, run full eval batch overnight. :white_check_mark:

josh_gold: Nice work. Please post the ticket link when ready and ping infra to run the quant export bisect.

anna_chen: will do. Thanks all :pray:
